Worm compost is an awesome fertiliser - here are some simple instructions to get started with worm composting

This image is similar to mine. http://www.readysetmom.com/.shared/image.html?/photos/uncategorized/2008/09/19/071008_012.jpg

The plans I used (which I cannot find right now) are similar to these. http://whatcom.wsu.edu/ag/compost/easywormbin.htm My bottom tub is different though.

The bottom tub is only a catch basin. I don't have any worms or scraps in it. It has holes on the sides at the top for ventilation but that is all. The valve is ...just add the valve people. So, so much easier! Only takes once spilling lechate all over you to make sure you do. The image I found has one but I haven't seen instructions about adding one. Just match your drill bit to the diameter and silicon around it. Don't go bigger with the bit though, just match it.

I added the valve and changed the bottom tub to a much taller tub because I was slow to empty the bottom catch tub one winter and lost my worms.

I have three top tubs though and rotate through those.

But If you really want to scrap everything, meats included, this is for you: http://www.thebiopod.com/ It uses soldier fly maggots. The adult flies do not eat as adults so no passing of diseases like house flies. And, their pheromones keep away house flies. I don't have one but have wanted this for years. There are some diy systems also if you search.

Then there is a combined system which seems an even better system. However, it must be very big. The soldier fly maggots and the redworms live at quite different temps. There is a video on youtube that I cannot find right now of a guy that has this system. He uses a huge stocktank though (maybe 100 gal, long with a plywood top and pvc vent...and also a valve) If I can find it later, I will throw it in as an edit. The nice part is no seperating scraps. EVERYTHING from the kitchen that will decompose just gets thrown in. More work to harvest soil but the lechate is where it is at! My plants go crazy on worm lechate.

The neat thing about the soldier fly maggots is that they render biologically problematic things (such as meat and even human waste although seriously not going to test that one) into biologically safe soil. There are some third world areas where they are using these systems to manage their waste and to provide better growing media which is scarce.

Edit: found it! Simple & Effective Worm Composting on your Homestead…: http://youtu.be/2SuBT7SukdI
I use the same stacked tub setup this year for the first time, it makes awesome compost and very quickly too. My plants were out of control they were growing so fast.

You are not kidding! My fushias and flowering plants in general go bonkers with it. I can't get enough of the stuff! I actually contemplated building a bigger system and grabbing scraps from neighbors. Alas, no where near enough time on my hands to get to that right now.
